sentences.text: Lingyuanosaurus was a small therizinosaur, a group of dinosaurs, measuring approximately 2.2 meters in length.
Based on a femur length of 200 mm, researchers estimated the weight of this animal to be about 12 kg.
The only known specimen includes various postcranial bones such as vertebrae, ribs, partial arm and leg bones, and claws.
This species is distinguished from other therizinosaurs by specific traits including a plate on dorsal vertebrae, unique vertebrae articulations, and a distinctively shaped ilium.
Researchers suggest that the Lingyuanosaurus specimen died before reaching full maturity.
Lingyuanosaurus possesses a proximodorsal lip on its claws, a feature found in basal therizinosaur taxa.
While the presence of a proximodorsal lip suggests claws could be used for feeding or digging, specific functions for Lingyuanosaurus claws remain unproposed.
The genus Lingyuanosaurus was formally described and named in 2019 by a team including Xi Yao, Chun-Chi Liao, Corwin Sullivan, and Xu Xing.
The generic name Lingyuanosaurus honors the city of Lingyuan and the Ancient Greek word for lizard.
The specific name sihedangensis refers to the town of Sihedang where the fossil was found.
The holotype specimen of Lingyuanosaurus was discovered near the town of Sihedang.
The species L. sihedangensis is known from fossils found within a layer of the Jehol Group.
The dietary habits of Lingyuanosaurus are unknown because no skull remains have been found.
It is possible that Lingyuanosaurus was herbivorous, as most known therizinosaurs were.
Despite only 45 out of over 300 character states being assignable due to incompleteness, analysis confirmed Lingyuanosaurus belongs to Therizinosauria.
Lingyuanosaurus is considered to represent an evolutionary transition within the therizinosaur lineage.
The original describers classified Lingyuanosaurus as a basal therizinosaur.
The Paleobiology Database lists Therizinosauria as the parent group for Lingyuanosaurus.
Lingyuanosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period in Liaoning Province, China.
The environment where Lingyuanosaurus lived had an average yearly temperature of 10°C, featuring relatively cold winters.
The paleoenvironment of the Jehol Group, where Lingyuanosaurus lived, featured warm and humid conditions with seasonal dry periods.
Lingyuanosaurus fossils were found within the Jehol biota, though the exact geological formation and precise age remain unknown.
Lingyuanosaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, between 133 and 120 million years ago, from the Barremian to the Aptian.
Fossils of Lingyuanosaurus have been found in what is now Asia.
The time range for Lingyuanosaurus is recorded as the Aptian, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
Researcher Mickey Mortimer suggests that Lingyuanosaurus might have been an oviraptorosaur instead of a therizinosaur.
